stances.claim: The November 22, 2011 SC resolution, though a triumph in principle, is extremely difficult to implement: at least four unresolved nitty-gritty issues — the 3% gross revenues already paid, the P1.33B proceeds from converted land, HLI's 'legitimate expenses,' and home lots valuation — combined with the deeply divided just compensation question, make the road 'still long and winding, full of slippery slopes.'
stances.rhetorical_move: implementation-complexity map: identifying at least four unresolved issues to temper post-ruling triumphalism

stances.claim: The SC should issue one omnibus resolution that includes all the justices' opinions and clearly shows where the majority stands — as done in prior contentious cases — to prevent the complexity of multiple divergent opinions from paralysing implementation.
stances.rhetorical_move: procedural-consolidation recommendation: omnibus resolution as the institutional tool for doctrinal clarification

notable_anecdotes: The July 5 to November 22 reversal: both resolutions penned by Justice Velasco — the first allowing stock ownership, the second invalidating it for parceling — a remarkable instance of the same justice writing two opposing SC resolutions on the same case within five months.

President Aquino's careful balancing act: as both the son of the hacienda's former owner (Cory Aquino's family/Cojuangco) and the PARC chair responsible for implementing the agrarian reform, he anchored his position on 'do not deplete capital' to justify just compensation — making him simultaneously the reform's executor and the landowners' indirect beneficiary.

The P1.33 billion windfall question: P1.25 billion from the 500 hectares converted to an industrial park and P80.5 million from 80.5 hectares sold for the SCTex at P100/sq m — a total more than enough to cover the 1989 appraisal of ~P1 billion — raising the question whether this should inure to the FWBs instead of requiring further payment.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes the SC's landmark November 22, 2011 resolution (penned by Justice Velasco) invalidating Hacienda Luisita's 1989 Stock Distribution Plan and ordering the parceling of 4,915.75 hectares among 6,296 qualified farmworker-beneficiaries -- partly reversing the July 5, 2011 Velasco decision that had allowed stock ownership and 3% gross revenues. While all 14 participating justices unanimously upheld the constitutional 'land-to-the-tiller' principle, they were deeply divided on just compensation: the six-justice majority (Velasco, De Castro, Peralta, Del Castillo, Abad, Perez) fixed the reckoning date at November 21, 1989 (the PARC SDP approval, yielding less than P1 billion) as 'preliminary' subject to RTC revisit; Justice Sereno reckoned the taking on January 2, 2006 (potentially many times higher); and Justice Bersamin (joined by Reyes and Bernabe) left the date to DAR, LandBank, and the Special Agrarian Court. CJ identifies at least four additional unresolved issues: accounting for 3% gross revenues already paid; whether the P1.33 billion from the converted industrial park and SCTex sale (more than enough to cover the 1989 appraisal) should inure to FWBs; computing HLI's 'legitimate taxes and expenses'; and valuing home lots. He notes the PARC (chaired by President Aquino who is simultaneously the son of the landowners' family and the reform's executor) plus DAR and LandBank must implement a 'long and winding' resolution, and recommends the Court issue an omnibus resolution clearly showing where the majority stands to prevent the complexity of divergent opinions from paralyzing implementation.
